_note: Authored mnemonics and illustration scenes. `rank` is the join key into src/domain/vocabulary/data/vocabulary.json (unique across all 4147 ranked entries; `thai` is NOT unique — 139 spellings repeat). Only `mnemonic` is merged into vocabulary.json and shipped to the browser; everything else is build-time input for scripts/generate-mnemonic-images.py. Style, aspect ratio, quality and negative prompt live in that script, never here.

_tone_glyphs.—: mid — flat, sits in the middle
_tone_glyphs.▁: low — flat, sits at the bottom

entries.mnemonic: A SWAT team smashes through the door, rifles up — then the lead officer lowers his weapon, presses his palms together and says softly, "sa-WAT-dee." The whole squad copies him. Even a raid starts with hello. (— levels out flat and calm on dee)
entries.headline: Sa-WAT-dee.
entries.scene: Interior of a small Thai apartment, splintered front door hanging open. Four armoured SWAT officers have just burst in; the lead officer at centre has lowered his rifle to his side and pressed his palms together in a wai greeting, head bowed, expression gentle. The three officers behind him are copying the gesture, rifles down, looking sheepish. Dust and daylight pour through the broken doorway behind them.

entries.mnemonic: A market vendor holds up a mango; the customer points at his own chest — "MY?" — voice climbing at the end the way an English question does. That climb is the question: ไหม turns any sentence into one. (↑ rising, the voice lifts like an eyebrow)
entries.headline: MY?
entries.scene: Bustling Thai street market at golden hour. A smiling vendor in an apron holds a ripe mango out across her fruit stall. Facing her, a young foreign traveller points at his own chest with both index fingers, eyebrows raised high, mouth open in an exaggerated questioning expression. Baskets of tropical fruit and hanging bulbs frame them.

entries.mnemonic: The same "my?" as ไหม — but shouted across a noisy bar, so the voice snaps up high and stays there instead of gliding. มั้ย is what friends say; ไหม is its polite written twin. (▲ high and flat-topped, a quick shout)
entries.headline: MY!
entries.scene: Crowded noisy Thai bar at night, packed with people. In the foreground a young man leans over a table, hands cupped around his mouth, shouting across the room toward a friend. The friend at the far side cups a hand behind his ear, squinting to hear. Neon signage, condensation on beer bottles, motion and crowd blur between them.

entries.mnemonic: A man sinks into a hammock and waves lazily — "sa-baaai" — a long drowsy bye as he drifts off. Nothing hurts, nothing to do. (— the second syllable stretches out level and relaxed)
entries.headline: sa-baaai…
entries.scene: A man lying back in a woven hammock strung between two coconut palms on a quiet Thai beach, one arm hanging loose and waving a slow lazy goodbye, eyes half closed, utterly relaxed. A cold drink rests in the sand beneath him. Calm turquoise sea and soft afternoon light behind.

entries.mnemonic: ไหน and ไหม are twins with the same rising climb — only the first sound differs. ไหม (M) asks "is it so?"; ไหน (N) asks "where?". Picture two identical signposts at a fork: the M arm points at a question mark, the N arm points at a map. Same rise in the voice, different letter, different question. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as the eyes search)
entries.scene: A weathered wooden signpost at a fork in a dirt road in rural Thailand, with two identical arms pointing opposite ways. The left arm carries a large carved question mark; the right arm carries a small rolled map pinned to it. A lone traveller with a backpack stands at the fork, hand shading his eyes, looking from one arm to the other. Rice paddies and distant hills, warm late light.

entries.mnemonic: She asks for chilli and the cook reaches for the whole jar. "Nòi!" — voice dropping low as she pinches her fingers a centimetre apart. Just a bit. (▁ low and small, the voice shrinks with the gesture)
entries.headline: Nòi!
entries.scene: A street food stall. The cook, grinning, is tipping an enormous jar of dried red chilli flakes toward a bowl of noodles. Across the counter a woman lunges forward with one hand raised in alarm, her other hand pinching thumb and forefinger a tiny distance apart. Steam, woks, stacked bowls, night market lights.

entries.mnemonic: A tow truck is hauling your car away. You sprint after it shouting "How much?! — tâo-rài!" and the driver leans out and holds up a single loaf of rye bread: that's the price. TOW plus RYE, and you never forget asking what it costs. (↓ falls hard on tâo, then drops low again on rài)
entries.headline: tâo-rài?!
entries.scene: A yellow tow truck driving away down a city street with a small car hoisted on its hook. A man in office clothes sprints after it, briefcase flying open, one arm outstretched and mouth wide open mid-shout. The driver leans out of the cab window holding up a single dark loaf of rye bread like a price tag. Motion blur, exhaust, late afternoon.

entries.mnemonic: An old janitor lifts a keyring so heavy it needs both hands — hundreds of keys fanning out like a metal peacock. Someone asks the only sensible question: "Kìi?" How many keys? (▁ low and flat, a short blunt question)
entries.headline: Kìi?
entries.scene: A dim school corridor. An elderly janitor in overalls hoists an enormous iron keyring with both hands, hundreds of keys fanned out from it in a huge glinting spray. A young student stands beside him staring up at it, one finger raised as if beginning to count. Long shafts of light from classroom windows.

entries.mnemonic: A small boy grabs an enormous weathered hand — a bear's paw of a hand — and says "Phôo." The hand belongs to his father, and it swallows his whole fist. (↓ falling, warm and settled)
entries.headline: Phôo.
entries.scene: Close view of a small boy's hand gripping the huge weathered calloused hand of his father, whose forearm fills the frame. The boy, about five, looks up with total trust; the father, a broad Thai labourer in a faded work shirt, looks down at him with a quiet smile. Warm kitchen light, out-of-focus home interior behind.

entries.mnemonic: A man raises his glass and intones "dɯɯm…" like a funeral bell — the last drink before DOOM. The trick is the lips: say DOOM while grinning, lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward, and you land the Thai vowel exactly. (▁ low and heavy, like the glass coming back down on the table)
entries.headline: dɯɯm…
entries.scene: A lone man at a long empty banquet table in a candlelit hall, raising a heavy glass in a solemn toast, grinning oddly wide as he does it. Behind him a huge cracked bronze bell hangs in the shadows. Guttering candles, long shadows, a sense of last things.

entries.mnemonic: A fortune teller peers over her cards, jabs a finger at you and says "Ah — YOU!" She has guessed your age to the year. aa-yú is the number of years you have. (↓ the second syllable snaps down on YOU)
entries.headline: Ah — YOU!
entries.scene: A fortune teller's booth draped in red cloth. An old woman with rings on every finger leans across a spread of cards and jabs one finger directly at the viewer, eyes wide with certainty. On the table beside the cards sits a small ornate abacus with a row of beads pushed across. Candles, incense smoke, deep shadows.

entries.mnemonic: Two brothers stand back to back to settle who is taller. The taller one is P — top of the list — "Phîi" — and his hand comes down flat on his brother's head to prove it. (↓ falling, the hand settles the matter)
entries.headline: Phîi.
entries.scene: Two Thai brothers standing back to back in a living room, comparing heights. The taller older one has reached up and over to lay his hand flat on top of his younger brother's head, smirking. The younger one stands on tiptoe, scowling, arms folded. A doorframe behind them is marked with pencil height lines.

entries.mnemonic: The little one pipes up — "Nóng!" — high and bright, the small voice that always goes up at the end and always wants in. He is the one still waiting to grow. (▲ high, a small bright voice)
entries.headline: Nóng!
entries.scene: A small child jumping up with one arm stretched high, beaming, trying to be included in a group of older kids who are standing in a huddle above him. He is clearly the smallest by a head. Sunlit Thai schoolyard, dusty ground, green trees behind.

entries.mnemonic: It is noon and nothing is happening. He lies flat and the afternoon goes on and on — "nooon" — never rising, never falling. (— completely level; the voice lies down too)
entries.headline: nooon…
entries.scene: A man asleep flat on his back on a wooden bench under a shop awning in the middle of a blazing hot day, hat over his face, one arm hanging off the side. A wall clock behind him reads exactly twelve. Empty sun-bleached street, hard midday shadows, heat haze.

entries.mnemonic: You suggest something ridiculous. Your friend shakes her head once and sets a heavy rock down on the table between you. Solid as a rock: no, definitely not, don't even think it. (▁ low and flat, the last word on the matter)
entries.headline: …ròok.
entries.scene: Two friends at a small café table. One leans forward mid-sentence, hands open, pleading. The other has just set a heavy grey river stone down on the tabletop between them with a thud, and is shaking her head once, eyebrows raised, utterly unmoved. Coffee cups rattle slightly. Warm café interior.

entries.mnemonic: A chef scans a row of identical mangoes, then slaps one down on the board — "nîi lɛ̀!" — that one. The word is over before it starts, cut off short like the slap itself. (▁ low and clipped, stopped dead at the end)
entries.headline: …lɛ̀!
entries.scene: A market chef's hands above a wooden board, having just slapped one mango down hard onto it; the other identical mangoes are lined up untouched behind. Slight motion blur on the striking hand, a puff of disturbed flour or dust rising from the board. Overhead market lighting, close crop.

entries.mnemonic: Take STRONG and knock the S off the front: troŋ. A soldier marches dead straight down a painted line, jaw set, refusing to deviate an inch. Strong and straight are the same idea here. (— flat and level, like the line he is walking)
entries.headline: troŋ!
entries.scene: A soldier in parade uniform marching precisely along a freshly painted white line down the centre of a wide road, back rigid, gaze fixed dead ahead. The line runs away from him to a vanishing point. Onlookers stand well back on both kerbs. Bright hard sunlight, sharp shadows.

entries.mnemonic: A shopkeeper slaps a new price tag over the old one — a LOT has come off. lót is the cut itself: prices, speed, weight, volume, anything that comes down. (↓ falls sharply, like the price)
entries.headline: lót!
entries.scene: A shopfront window. A grinning shopkeeper on a step stool slaps a huge red price tag over an old one, the old higher number still half visible underneath. Shoppers outside the glass are pressing in to look. Bright commercial lighting, sale banners, festive clutter.

entries.mnemonic: Ask a Thai shopkeeper what she does and she will tell you she runs this place. A ráan is a shop — the thing you run. The word and the job are the same sound. (▲ high, said with pride)
entries.headline: My ráan.
entries.scene: A proud middle-aged Thai woman standing in the open doorway of her small neighbourhood shop, arms folded, chin up, framed by shelves of goods stacked floor to ceiling behind her. Hand-painted signage above the door, a scooter parked outside, early morning light down the street.

entries.mnemonic: You jàai for your chai. The two words sit almost on top of each other — the drink and the paying for it — so every cup you buy is a free rehearsal. (▁ low, the flat sound of coins going down on the counter)
entries.headline: jàai for chai.
entries.scene: A tea stall counter. A customer's hand places a small stack of coins down on the wooden counter beside a steaming glass of milky orange Thai iced tea. The vendor's hand is reaching for the coins from the other side. Close low-angle crop on the counter, warm steam, sunlit street behind.

entries.mnemonic: Every career ladder has the same thing at the top: a chief. aa-chîip is the whole ladder — the trade you follow and where it leads. (↓ falls firmly on the second syllable, the weight of a title)
entries.headline: aa-chîip.
entries.scene: A long ladder rising out of an open-plan office floor and up through a skylight, with workers in different uniforms — cook, nurse, mechanic, engineer — climbing it at different heights. At the very top rung stands a figure in a chief's peaked cap, silhouetted against bright sky. Upward perspective.

entries.mnemonic: The waiter refuses to take a spoken order — everything must be sung. The customer stands, hand on heart, and sings her dinner across the restaurant. You sàng what you sung. (▁ low and flat, even when sung badly)
entries.headline: sàng!
entries.scene: A restaurant dining room. A woman has risen from her table, one hand on her heart and the other flung out theatrically, singing her order toward a waiter who stands to attention with notepad raised, delighted. Other diners turn to watch. Warm chandelier light, white tablecloths.

entries.mnemonic: Whatever you bought, you bought it in bàat. The English past tense and the Thai currency are the same sound, and the one always follows the other. (▁ low and flat, the sound of a note being laid down)
entries.headline: bàat.
entries.scene: A close overhead view of a market transaction: a hand laying purple and green Thai banknotes down onto a wooden counter, beside a wrapped parcel tied with string that has just been paid for. The vendor's hands rest on the parcel, about to push it across. Warm stall lighting.

entries.mnemonic: A cat on a windowsill lifts its nose, reads the air and knows the rain is coming an hour before you do. aa-kàat is both the air and what it is doing — weather. (▁ the second syllable settles low, like the cat)
entries.headline: aa-kàat.
entries.scene: A cat sitting upright on an open wooden windowsill, nose lifted and eyes half closed, whiskers catching the wind. Beyond the window a dark bank of monsoon cloud is rolling in over rooftops while the street below is still in sunshine. Curtains lifting in the draught.

entries.mnemonic: A cat strolls along the table edge and calmly nudges a tumbler into the void. CAT — OW! — and the glass is gone. Say those two together and you have kɛ̂ɛo. (↓ falls, the way the glass does)
entries.headline: CAT — OW!
entries.scene: A cat standing on a dining table with one paw extended, having just pushed a drinking glass over the edge; the glass is caught mid-fall in the air below, water arcing out of it. The cat looks directly at the viewer, entirely unbothered. Sunlit dining room, wooden table, shallow depth of field.
